text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Demonstrators protesting over annulment of election results celebrate Orthodox Christmas Eve in front of St Sava Cathedral in Belgrade. Serbian Patriarch Pavle holds midnight mass.

- Students protesting election annulments met Yugoslav army chief General Momcilo Perisic and Serbian Interior Minister Zoran Sokolovic. Army promises not to go out on the streets while police say they will act "according to the law".

- German mark is realistically worth 5.5 dinars at the moment (3.3 dinars according to the official exchange rate), says economist Miroljub Labus who also predicts speedier drop of the dinar's value in a month or two.
- Commercial banks out of cash even though circulation in the money mass has grown amid speculation cash has been diverted to street dealers, pushing up the value of German mark in black market.
- Ready money in circulation increased by 486 million dinars in October with no visible effect on bank accounts which remain depleted. No November figures are available.
- National Bank of Yugoslavia closes Slavia bank and Monte Rojal Bank, effective December 28, 1996.
- Serbian Petrol industry NIS-Jugopetrol will import 2.6 million tonnes of crude in 1997 which is double last year's figure, says general manager Dragan Tomic.
- No deals can be made on the northern Bosnian Serb town of Brcko, says Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic.
- Belgrade mayor Nebojisa Covic neither denies nor confirms rumours about his resignation and expects to say something on the subject after the holidays.

- Member of the European parliament transport commission Brian Simpson talks to Milomir Minic, Yugoslav Parliament Lower House Speaker, stressing Yugoslavia's importance in development of transport in southeastern Europe.
